page.title: Release readiness
page.purpose: Walk the owner from no account to a production listing, naming at every rung what is done, what is blocked, and what only a person can do.

priorities.statement: Rungs are ordered, and a later rung never reports ready while an earlier one is not.
priorities.notes: Order is the information. A ladder whose rungs can be read independently is just a checklist.

priorities.statement: Each rung states plainly whether the ramp can complete it or only the owner can.
priorities.notes: Registration, identity verification, and payment are irreducibly human. Implying otherwise wastes the owner's time.

priorities.statement: Each rung shows its cost where one exists.
priorities.notes: A $25 registration is a decision, not a task. The surface should not hide that it costs money.

priorities.statement: Dated obligations are shown with their dates.
priorities.notes: Target API 36 by 31 August 2026 and developer verification from 30 September 2026 are deadlines, not preferences.

priorities.statement: Rung state is re-probed, never read from a stored flag.
priorities.notes: A lapsed or revoked account must not continue to read as satisfied.

elements.name: Readiness rungs
elements.description: The ordered ladder from no account to production listing. Array order is the dependency order.

elements.name: Rung state
elements.description: The probed state of one rung, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Completed by
elements.description: Whether the ramp can complete this rung or only the owner can.

elements.name: Cost
elements.description: The monetary cost of a rung where one exists, shown as part of the rung rather than in documentation.

elements.name: Next action
elements.description: The single action that advances the first unsatisfied rung.

elements.name: Deadline
elements.description: The dated external obligation attached to a rung, where one exists.

states.description: Rung states are being probed; none are asserted yet.
No Google account has been configured at all, so no rung can even be probed. Distinct from a probed-and-unsatisfied ladder.
Some rungs were probed and others could not be reached; the unprobed ones are explicitly unknown rather than assumed unsatisfied.
Rung state is from an old probe. Age is shown, because a lapsed account must not continue to read as satisfied.
The readiness probe failed. Reported as a failure rather than as an unsatisfied ladder.
No Play Console account exists. The first rung is the only actionable one and every later rung is explicitly blocked by it.
Registration is complete and developer verification is submitted but not granted. Distinguishes 'waiting on Google' from 'waiting on you'.
Every rung satisfied; the internal testing track is available.

claims.statement: The ladder is presented in dependency order, so the first unsatisfied rung is the first one an owner reads.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-009. Order is the information. A ladder that can report a later rung ready out of order is not modelling a dependency, it is displaying independent flags.

claims.statement: Every rung shows its state and whether the ramp or the owner completes it.
claims.rationale: The purpose of the surface is to tell the owner what to do next; conflating 'blocked on you' with 'blocked on the system' defeats it.

claims.statement: A rung that costs money displays that cost.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-009. A $25 registration is a decision, not a task. The surface should not hide that it costs money.

claims.statement: A rung carrying a dated external obligation displays that date.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-002, S2A-P0-008. Target API 36 and developer verification are deadlines with real consequences; a rung that hides its date cannot be planned against.

claims.statement: An unstarted ladder presents the single next action that advances it.
claims.rationale: The ladder exists to answer 'what do I do now'. Showing six blocked rungs without one action does not answer it.

claims.statement: A ladder awaiting a Google decision renders distinguishably from one awaiting an owner action.
claims.rationale: Verification review can take days. An owner who cannot tell these apart will either wait on themselves or act on something already submitted.

claims.statement: Rung state shown to the owner reflects a probe rather than a stored completion flag, so a lapsed or revoked account stops reading as satisfied.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-009. This is a data-provenance property that cannot be observed from the rendered tree alone; it needs a human or an integration test to attest.
